name: Cell–Cell Coupling
description: Paper §Cell–cell coupling (no dedicated figure). Two cell agents are wired to ONE shared environmental nutrient store: each senses the pool and depletes it, so their interfaces are coupled not only through shared state but through CONSTRAINT — one cell's uptake reshapes the other's viability. DRAFT: typed ports + contract, no dynamics — node config carries ONLY the timestep. cell_a_proc addresses local:CellAgent and cell_b_proc addresses local:RivalCellAgent: two draft roles with IDENTICAL ports/contract (see interfaces.py), so an env can hand each cell a different handler/config (the compiler keys handler lookup by draft address, so two nodes sharing one draft address cannot receive different handler configs — see handler_envs.py). Competitive asymmetry (cell_a stronger than cell_b) and cross-feeding symmetry both live entirely in the env layer (law 4: swap the env, not this composite).
